about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Repo Minions, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_strand.py (class Promises) refuses a version while a row due in it has no test, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be named in the plan next to the codon.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which kind of machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the skill is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: GitHub's documentation says a lock on an account can block GitHub Actions. A run that GitHub does not start ends 'startup_failure' with zero jobs, and no runner of the person's can change that. A test on another repository proves nothing about this one.
rows.promise: Before installing, look tests whether GitHub creates jobs for THIS repository and names a zero-job startup_failure as an account or repository matter; setup stops there and the skill is never offered as a way around it.

rows.seen: Seen: self-hosted runners attached to public repositories, guarded only by a same-repository condition in the workflow file and by approval of outside contributors. A fork's pull request runs its own copy of the workflow file, so the condition is not a boundary. Repositories also changed visibility after their runners were set up.
rows.promise: Refuse a repository that is not private, at the tool, and hold its runners within one watch interval when it stops being private.
rows.proven: 2026-11-23, a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 virtual machine and the private proof repository, proven by the owner's word, seen once: unsteered, `look` of a really public repository said `stop … is public: Repo Minions never puts a runner on a repository that is not private …`, exit 2, nothing changed. Steered, the same steer as row R62: the watch's one privacy read was answered public by a wrapper put in front of gh (from 03:20:34Z to 03:29:27Z UTC, and three shorter times), everything else real: the watch's first pass held the runner and took it off the repository on GitHub's side once idle, status began with a stop saying every job is refused, a real job asking for our labels was refused, and `resume --private-again` then setup brought it back. Not seen: a repository really turned public with a runner on it, which is not done, by rule.

rows.proven: 2026-11-23, a stock Ubuntu 22.04.5 virtual machine and the private proof repository, proven by the owner's word, seen once, on the fix of row R84: during a real job, the runner's listener was held with a stop signal (SIGSTOP) sent by the person's own sudo, from 10:15:12Z to 10:17:27Z (UTC), as a stalled process is held; the tool's files were not touched. While GitHub said offline and busy and a job process ran here, status said `warn the two sides disagree`, with both sides; idle was said only after the signal to go on (SIGCONT), once both sides agreed (`ok idle`), and the job passed. Steered: the listener's hold. Unsteered, the two sides were never caught apart (status read every 2 to 3 seconds through a job).

Steer 2: the saved earlier text altered by hand ("Self-hosted runners (until further notice).") with its dates set back 8 days; the weekly pass journaled `cost rule changed GitHub's list changed since 2026-11-15T12:25:12Z`, the next `status` began with `warn GitHub's billing page changed what it says about self-hosted runners: read 2026-11-15T12:25:12Z, it said "…"; read 2026-11-23T12:25:17Z, it says "…". Read it yourself before relying on it: …`, and the status after it did not say it again. Not seen: GitHub's page really changing.

rows.seen: Seen many times over months: restarts of machines that carry runners (planned test restarts, a system updater, a reset) cancelled the job running at that moment; the safe practice that grew up was to hold the runner, wait for its job, and hand it back only as 'online and idle', read after the restart.

rows.proven: Seen twice, a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 virtual machine and the private proof repository: the night of 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 05:03-05:10 UTC (held, waited for the job, 'safe to restart now' only after it ended, a job queued during the hold, the hold lifted by itself after the reboot, the next job ran).

rows.seen: Seen: a laptop used as a runner ran hot and throttled under a job, its disk went read-only under load, and runners on a flaky home uplink lost their jobs; a person's own computer is often a laptop that sleeps, closes its lid, runs on battery and changes networks.
rows.promise: A laptop is named before setup with what it means; on battery the runners are held by default; a sleep during a job is put off where the OS allows and what cannot be put off is said; after a wake or network change the runner is seen back on both sides.

rows.seen: GitHub's documentation (read 2026-11-22): a self-hosted runner is removed automatically if it has not connected for more than 14 days. Seen on test machines: runners whose registrations had been removed on the server side restarted in a loop on refused credentials after the machine came back.
rows.promise: A runner GitHub removed is named plainly, its service does not restart in a loop, and setup registers it again with the person's login.
rows.proven: 2026-11-23, a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 virtual machine and the private proof repository, proven by the owner's word, seen once. Steered: the runner's registration was removed by our own call to GitHub's API (02:57:30Z UTC), standing in for GitHub's removal after 14 days offline. The runner's answer was GitHub's own ("registration has been deleted"); its listener retried once, then stopped the service with no retry (NRestarts 0); the watch said `GitHub no longer lists` the runner; setup registered it again in place, folders and labels kept, both sides online. Learned later: how soon an old listener stops itself is not fixed, so setup now stops what is left first. Not seen: GitHub's own 14-day removal.
